checks: Original 655fcaee47bd2237 §1 has the same gauge argument and a triangular boundary-fixed exception; the frozen proof specifies an equal-area partition.

After translation the maps are linear and their body inclusions imply gauge nonincrease. The nonnegative differences are continuous on the body and have zero averaged integral. Positivity of all weights and full support imply each difference vanishes everywhere on the body.

Positive homogeneity extends gauge preservation to all vectors; trivial kernel gives invertibility, and the gauge unit sublevel set is consequently preserved bijectively. The determinant follows from volume.

For the two boundary-fixed triangle maps, directly compute absolute determinants 1/2. Their images form the two triangle pieces and their pushforwards have density two on those pieces. The equal-weight mixture therefore reproduces uniform area.
